title: Gameworld Parameter Set
description: The set of all map and world parameters of a foundation, grouped by region generation stage. A parameter that is left out keeps its default. Section numbers refer to docs/map-generation.md, and those marked society to docs/society-generation.md.

$schema.description: The address of this schema, so an editor can show help for the file. Ignored when the file is loaded.

Siting.description: Sited stage: the three levels of cells, the ocean seeds and the elevation types (§3, §4, §5.1, §8).

RegionGridSizeKm.description: Grid spacing of the region level in km: the size of a region (§4).

RegionJitter.description: How far a region site may lie from the centre of its grid square: 0 gives a square grid, 1 lets the site be anywhere in its square (§3.1).

ZoneGridSizeKm.description: Grid spacing of the zone level in km. The sizes are kept nested: it is clamped to between 1/16 and 1/1.5 of the region size (§4).

ZoneJitter.description: How far a zone site may lie from the centre of its grid square: 0 gives a square grid, 1 lets the site be anywhere in its square (§3.1).

ZoneWarp.description: Border warp of the zone level, in cell sizes. 0 leaves the borders of zone cells unwarped. It affects which zone cell owns a patch cell (§3.2, §4).

ZoneWarpFrequency.description: Warp noise cycles per zone cell. Only used when ZoneWarp is above 0 (§3.2).

PatchGridSizeKm.description: Grid spacing of the patch level in km. It is clamped to between 1/16 and 1/1.5 of the zone size (§4).

PatchJitter.description: How far a patch site may lie from the centre of its grid square: 0 gives a square grid, 1 lets the site be anywhere in its square (§3.1).

PatchWarp.description: Border warp of the patch level, in cell sizes. Coastlines and zone and region borders run along patch borders, so this gives all of them their wavy shape. 0 gives straight borders (§3.2, §4).

PatchWarpFrequency.description: Warp noise cycles per patch cell: lower gives broader waves in the borders (§3.2).

NestLevels.description: Classify a point through its patch only (point → patch → zone → region), so zone borders, region borders and coastlines all run along patch borders. Only true is supported: every later layer assumes nesting (§4).

OceanSeedsPerRegion.description: How many of the zone cells it owns each region chooses as ocean seeds: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max. More seeds give more sea (§5.1).

ElevationWeights.description: Relative weights of the four land elevation types, drawn per zone cell. Whole numbers; with the defaults 5 of 13 zone cells are Flat Land (§8).

Outline.description: Outlined stage: ocean links, ocean expansion and zone mergers (§5.2, §5.3, §6.1).

OceanLinkChance.description: Chance that an ocean seed makes one link, to its nearest other ocean seed. Tested when the seed does not make two links. Every zone cell under a link becomes ocean (§5.2).

OceanDoubleLinkChance.description: Chance that an ocean seed makes two links, to its two nearest other ocean seeds. Tested first (§5.2).

OceanLinkRangeRegions.description: How many regions away an ocean seed looks for seeds to link to: 2 is a 5 × 5 block of regions. A region can be Outlined when all regions within this range + 5 rings are Sited, so a larger range makes every lookup reach further (§5.2).

OceanExpansionFrom.description: Which ocean zone cells expand in the first pass. Linked: every zone cell on a link, so a lone ocean seed stays a sea of one zone cell. All: every ocean zone cell, lone seeds too (§5.3).

OceanExpansionPasses.description: Number of ocean expansion passes. Each pass after the first expands from the zone cells the previous pass converted. More passes give more sea; 0 turns expansion off (§5.3).

OceanExpansionWeights.description: Relative weights for an expanding zone cell converting 0, 1, 2 or 3 of its nearest land neighbours to ocean: four numbers in that order. A negative weight counts as 0 (§5.3).

ZoneMergersPerRegion.description: How many of the zone cells it owns each region chooses to merge into their nearest neighbour: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max. A merger that finds no neighbour on its side of the coast still counts (§6.1).

MergeAcrossCoast.description: Let a zone cell merge into its nearest neighbour even when one is land and the other ocean. Off by default: only land-land and ocean-ocean mergers are allowed (§6.1).

Detail.description: Detailed stage: patch mergers, rivers and lakes (§6.3, §10, §11).

PatchMergersPerZoneCell.description: How many of the patch cells it owns each zone cell chooses to merge into their nearest neighbour patch cell in the same zone: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max (§6.3).

Rivers.description: Rivers: grown per region with space colonization, from the sea into the land (§10).

AttractorsPerPatchCell.description: Attraction points scattered in every eligible patch cell. More give denser rivers. River sizes are flows divided by this number, so they read as patches drained (§10.1).

StepKm.description: Length of one growth step, which is one river segment, in km (§10).

InfluenceKm.description: An attractor pulls its nearest river node only within this radius, in km. Raised to at least 1.5 × the step. A large radius gives fewer, straighter rivers; a small one many independent branches (§10, §18.2).

KillKm.description: An attractor is reached once a river node is this close, in km. Raised to at least 1.05 × the step (§10).

RandomMotion.description: Weight of a random unit vector added to the direction of every growth step. 0 gives straight runs towards the attractors (§10.3).

Wander.description: How much of a step's random vector is inherited from the parent node, 0 to 1. Higher makes bends persist over several steps instead of wiggling (§10.3).

PerceptionConeDegrees.description: A river node is only pulled by attractors within ± half this angle of its heading, in degrees. It stops branches hooking back; 360 lets nodes see all round (§10.3).

MainStemDominance.description: A node that already has a child only sprouts a side branch if its own pulls are at least this share of the pulls on the stem beyond it. Higher removes more short side twigs; 0 turns it off (§10.5).

PullPower.description: Weight of one pull by its distance d relative to the influence radius. Normal: every pull has equal weight. Squared: (d / influence)², far attractors pull harder. Root: √(d / influence) (§10.3).

Inertia.description: Weight of the node's current heading in the direction of its next step. 0 is no inertia; higher gives straighter rivers (§10.3).

SkipCoastalPatchCells.description: Put no attractors in coastal patch cells. It keeps river mouths apart and gives the rivers a clear run from the coast into the interior (§10.1).

RiverPoorPrecipitationCutoffMm.description: A flat zone whose site gets less precipitation than this, in mm/yr, is river-poor: its patch cells get 0 or 1 attractor instead of the full number, it is drier for the biomes and it holds no lakes. Higher makes more of the flat zones dry plains (§10.1).

Lakes.description: Lakes: placed per region on the rivers (§11).

Frequency.description: Chance that a patch cell with a suitable river node gets a lake (§11).

MinSizeKm.description: Smallest lake in km, measured as the diameter of a circle of equal area (§11).

MaxSizeKm.description: Largest lake in km, measured as the diameter of a circle of equal area. Sizes are skewed towards small lakes (§11).

Elevation.description: Elevated stage: the height map and the biomes (§12, §13).

HeightMap.description: The height map: a raster per region, fitted to the rivers and the coast (§12).

ChannelSlope.description: River gradient at a flow of 1, in m/m. Higher gives steeper rivers, and with them higher land, since the land rises from the river beds (§12.2).

Concavity.description: Rivers flatten downstream as flow to the power −concavity: higher gives flatter large rivers. The default is 7/16; multiples of 1/16 are computed exactly (§12.2).

HillslopeMultiplier.description: Scales the hillslope of every elevation type (§12).

LevelFlatZones.description: How strongly zones with a river gradient factor below 1 (flat zones by default) are levelled towards the height of their lowest river entry, so they read as a plain at roughly one level. 0 turns levelling off (§12.2).

MountainBelts.description: Strength of the region-scale relief field, which makes groups of neighbouring zones rugged or gentle together. 0 turns it off (§12.1).

RegionRidgeM.description: Ridge height along region borders, in metres. Region borders are watersheds (§12.5).

BasinDivideM.description: Ridge height between two river systems, in metres (§12.5).

DetailNoise.description: Multiplier on the surface detail noise. 0 gives a smooth surface (§12.5).

ChannelDepthM.description: How deep rivers are cut below their bed profile, in metres (§12.6).

SeaDepthM.description: Sea depth 40 km or more from the coast, in metres (§12.5).

Hillslope.description: How steeply the land rises away from rivers and the coast, in m/m, per elevation type. This is what makes the land between the rivers a plain or a range (§12).

RiverGradientFactor.description: Multiplier on the river gradient, per elevation type. A type with a factor below 1 is levelled, see LevelFlatZones (§12.2).

Floodplain.description: Floodplain half-width as a function of the river bed height (§12).

Points.description: Control points of a monotone spline from river bed height to floodplain half-width. The half-width is constant beyond the end points and never less than 0.75 × the raster cell size (§12).

items.description: One control point: the floodplain half-width at a river bed height.

HalfWidthM.description: Floodplain half-width in metres at that bed height.

ScaleWithRiverSize.description: When on, the points give the half-width at a flow of 100 and other flows get × √(flow / 100), so big rivers get wide floodplains (§12).

Biomes.description: Biomes: one per land patch, from temperature and aridity, and the flora and fauna of a patch (§13).

Cooling.description: Control points of a monotone spline from height to the cooling of the Initial Temperature. Constant below the first point; above the last it continues along the last segment's slope. The defaults are much steeper than the real atmosphere, so land below 1000 m still gets cold highlands (§13.1).

items.description: One control point: the cooling at a height.

RiverPoorPrecipitationFactor.description: The precipitation of a patch in a river-poor flat zone is multiplied by this for the biomes. Lower makes the dry plains drier (§13.1).

MangroveMinTemperatureC.description: A coastal patch in a flat or lowland zone becomes Mangrove when it is at least this warm, in °C, and at least as wet as MangroveMinAridity (§13.2).

MangroveMinAridity.description: The smallest aridity (precipitation ÷ the dryness threshold of the temperature) at which a warm low coast becomes Mangrove. Below 0.5 is desert, 0.5 to 1 steppe, above 1 humid (§13.2).

VolcanoChance.description: The chance that a patch in a mountains zone is a Volcano, whatever its climate. 0 gives no volcanoes. The default gives about one Volcano in nine regions (§13.2).

FloraPerPatch.description: How many kinds of flora a patch gets: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max. A patch gets fewer when fewer kinds fit it (§13.4).

FaunaPerPatch.description: How many kinds of fauna a patch gets: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max. A patch gets fewer when fewer kinds fit it (§13.4).

Planning.description: Planned stage: Prospects for cities and towns, which of them are on show (§15), the potential population (society §3) and the factions (society §4).

ProspectsPerRegion.description: Prospects per region. Regions with little habitable land end up with fewer (§15.5).

CityProspectsPerRegion.description: How many of a region's Prospects are for cities, at most. The rest are for towns (§15.5).

SpacingKm.description: Smallest distance between two Prospects, in km. Prospects for cities keep 2.5 × this from each other. When a region cannot fit its Prospects the spacing is relaxed by 15 % at a time, down to one patch size (§15.5).

Weights.description: Weights of the five factors in the score of a patch. Only their proportions matter. A negative weight counts as 0; if all are 0 the plain mean is used (§15.4).

Resources.description: Weight of the resources factor: food, fresh water, building materials and fuel, fish and trade goods on and around the patch (§15.3).

Geography.description: Weight of the geography factor: buildable ground, waterside and defence (§15.3).

Trade.description: Weight of the trade factor: gateways (river mouths, harbours, heads of navigation, confluences) and how much of the region's food is within reach (§15.3).

Climate.description: Weight of the climate factor: a comfortable temperature and enough moisture (§15.3).

Prosperity.description: Weight of the prosperity factor: the Prosperity field at the spot (§15.3).

OneOnShowScoreSum.description: The sum of the scores of a region's Prospects at or below which only 1 of them is on show. The number on show grows evenly with the sum from here to AllOnShowScoreSum. Prospects on show are drawn on a map and connected by roads, river routes and sea lanes. With the defaults about 1 region in 20 shows a single Prospect and the median region shows 13 of its 20 (§15.6, §16).

AllOnShowScoreSum.description: The sum of the scores of a region's Prospects at or above which all of them are on show. With the defaults about 1 region in 10 shows all 20 (§15.6).

RichScore.description: A Prospect with at least this score (0 to 100) is Rich: a map draws it in gold. With the defaults about a quarter of the Prospects on show are Rich (§15.6, §17).

PoorScore.description: A Prospect with a score (0 to 100) below this is Poor: a map draws it in bronze. The ones between are Average, in silver. With the defaults about a fifth of the Prospects on show are Poor (§15.6, §17).

Population.description: The potential population of a region: how many persons its land can feed. The races that are on share it (society §3).

PersonsPerKm2.description: Persons per km² on land with a food supply of 1 at a middling Prosperity. The potential population of a patch is its area × this × its food supply × its Prosperity factor (society §3.1).

ProsperityEffect.description: How much the Prosperity field moves the potential population of a patch: the factor runs from 1 − this at the lowest Prosperity to 1 + this at the highest. 0 turns the effect of Prosperity off (society §3.1).

RacesPerRegion.description: The most races a region holds: its main races and its minority races. Only they share the potential population of the region. A number at or above the number of races that are on, with no minority races, gives every race its plain share (society §3.3).

MinorityRacesPerRegion.description: How many of the races of a region are minority races: the last places, which go to the race whose turn it is in the region. The other places go to the main races, the largest by their plain shares. Every race that is on has one turn per place in every 6 × 5 block of regions with the default 28 races (society §3.3).

RacesPerCity.description: The most races a city holds. They are races of its region: the largest around the Prospect, and a last one drawn with the minority races weighted up (society §5.1).

RacesPerTown.description: The most races a town holds. They are races of its region: the largest around the Prospect, and a last one drawn with the minority races weighted up (society §5.1).

MinorityMinPersons.description: How many persons of a race the land of a region must feed by the plain shares for the race to take a minority place there (society §3.3).

MinorityShare.description: The share of the potential population of a region that a minority race is lifted towards, 0 to 0.9. A minority race that already holds more keeps its share, and one that lives on a few patches only stays below it. 0 turns the lift off (society §3.4).

MinorityBoost.description: The factor on a minority race of the region in the draw for the last race of a city or a town. 1 gives it no advantage (society §5.1).

HinterlandShare.description: How much of the potential population of the whole region a city or a town draws on, beside the patch of its Prospect and the land patches around it, 0 to 1. It lets a race of the region that does not live nearby into the city or town (society §5.1).

Factions.description: The factions of a region: its ruling faction, its opposition and its lesser factions, from the races, the biomes, the resources and the wealth of the region (society §4).

RacePower.description: How much the size of a race counts when the lead race of the ruling faction is drawn: the share of the race in the persons of the region is raised to this power. With the default the largest race leads in about 6 regions in 10 and a minority race in 1 in 100. A higher number makes the largest race lead more often (society §4.4).

Sharpness.description: How much the land decides the type of the ruling faction: the fit of each type is raised to this power. 1 lets the leaning of the races decide more; a high number makes the type with the best fit rule nearly always (society §4.4).

BaseFit.description: The fit of each type as the ruler in a land that says nothing for it, 0 to 1. The land moves the fit from here up to 1. A higher base makes the type rule more regions (society §4.4).

Family.description: Value for the type Family: a house and its household.

Race.description: Value for the type Race: a people.

Vocation.description: Value for the type Vocation: a trade.

Belief.description: Value for the type Belief: a faith.

Magic.description: Value for the type Magic: the arcane.

Place.description: Value for the type Place: a town or a valley that rules itself.

Tension.description: The weights of the five terms of the tension of a region. The tension runs from 0 to their sum, 1 with the defaults (society §4.5).

Contest.description: Weight of the contest: the land and the races would as well carry another kind of ruler (society §4.5).

RoughLand.description: Weight of rough land: hills and mountains shelter those who do not obey (society §4.5).

RivalSeat.description: Weight of a rival seat: a second Prospect on show nearly as good as the best, and far from it (society §4.5).

PreciousFinds.description: Weight of precious finds: silver and lead, gold, gems and pearls (society §4.5).

PoorLand.description: Weight of poor land: Poor Prospects, and rich and poor Prospects side by side (society §4.5).

OppositionTension.description: The tension from which a region has an opposition. With the default about 4 regions in 10 have an opposition; 0.4 gives 6 in 10 and 0.6 gives 2 in 10 (society §4.5).

TensionJitter.description: The width of the random part of the tension: a number from minus half this to plus half this is added, drawn per region. 0 makes the tension alone decide (society §4.5).

OppositionMinPersons.description: The persons a region needs to hold an opposition (society §4.5).

Cleavage.description: Which type opposes which ruler: for each type of the ruling faction, the weight of each type as its opposition. A crown is opposed by a rival house first, a people by another people, a guild by a rival guild, a faith by a sect or by the mages, a free town by a lord who wants it (society §4.6).

PersonsPerLesserFaction.description: The persons a region needs for each lesser faction: a region holds at most its persons divided by this, rounded down (society §4.7).

MaxLesserFactions.description: The most lesser factions a region holds (society §4.7).

LesserFit.description: The lowest fit, 0 to 1, with which a kind of lesser faction is taken. A lower number gives more lesser factions (society §4.7).

LesserJitter.description: The width of the random part of the fit of a kind of lesser faction: a number from minus half this to plus half this is added, drawn per region and kind (society §4.7).

FavouriteColourWeight.description: The weight of the first favourite colour of the lead race when a colour of a faction is drawn. The second favourite has half of it, the third a third and so on (society §4.9).

OtherColourWeight.description: The weight of a colour that is not a favourite colour of the lead race when a colour of a faction is drawn. 0 keeps a faction to the favourite colours of its lead race; a higher number gives more factions a colour of their own (society §4.9).

TakenColourFactor.description: What the weight of a colour is multiplied by in the draw for the main colour when a faction in a lower slot of the region already has it as its main colour. With the default 0 no two factions of a region share a main colour while there are colours left, so a ruler and its opposition never fly the same banner. 1 lets them share a main colour freely (society §4.9).

ColourContrast.description: How much the lightness of the secondary colour must differ from that of the main colour, 0 to 1, so that the one stands out on the other. The lightness of a colour is (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B) / 255. When no colour differs that much, the secondary colour is drawn from every other colour (society §4.9).

Indices.description: The ranges the indices of a region are read through: each index runs from 0 at Low to 1 at High. The defaults are about the 10th and the 90th percentile of generated regions, so a change to the map parameters can call for new ranges (society §4.3).

Grain.description: Grain: the mean amount of grain on the land of the region (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Livestock.description: Half of the index herd: the mean amount of livestock (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Horses.description: Half of the index herd: the mean amount of horses and pack animals (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

OpenLand.description: Open: the share of the land in Cold steppe, Temperate grassland, Savanna, Cold desert, Hot desert, Thorn scrub and Tundra (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Forest.description: Forest: the share of the land in the six forest biomes, Mangrove and Woodland & shrubland (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

ColdLand.description: Cold: the share of the land in Ice & snow, Tundra and Boreal forest (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

DryLand.description: Dry: the share of the land in Hot desert, Cold desert, Cold steppe and Thorn scrub (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

RoughLand.description: Rough: the share of the land in Hills zones plus 1.5 times the share in Mountains zones (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

TradeFactor.description: Half of the index trade: the best Trade factor of a Prospect on show (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Harbours.description: Half of the index trade: the number of Prospects on show with a harbour or a navigable river mouth (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Prosperity.description: Half of the index wealth: the mean Prosperity factor of the Prospects of the region (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

RichProspects.description: Half of the index wealth: the number of Rich Prospects on show (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

ProspectsOnShow.description: Urban: the number of Prospects on show (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Ore.description: Ore: the shares of the land with a listed amount of iron ore, copper ore, tin, silver and lead, gold, gems and pearls and salt, added (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Precious.description: Precious: the shares of the land with a listed amount of silver and lead, gold and gems and pearls, added (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Supernatural.description: Arcane: the mean over the land of how far the Supernatural field lies above 60, from 0 at 60 to 1 at 100 (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Persons.description: People: the persons of the region (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

SmallRegion.description: Small: the persons of the region, read the other way round: the index is 1 at Low and below and 0 at High and above (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

LargestRace.description: Mixed: the share of the largest race in the persons of the region, read the other way round: the index is 1 at Low and below and 0 at High and above (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

PoorProspects.description: Poor: the share of the Prospects on show that are Poor (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

UnevenProsperity.description: Uneven: the highest Prosperity factor of a Prospect on show minus the lowest (society §4.3).

Low.description: The value at and below which the index is 0.

High.description: The value at and above which the index is 1.

Names.description: The name of a region: when a region is small or large to the region-name generator (society §4.10).

SmallRegionPersons.description: A region with fewer persons than this is small. When the lead race of its ruling faction is human, its name can end in Duchy, Province, Len or County. With the defaults about 1 region in 4 is small (society §4.10).

LargeRegionPersons.description: A region with more persons than this is large. When the lead race of its ruling faction is human, its name can start with Gran, Grand or Great. With the defaults about 1 region in 5 is large (society §4.10).

Settlement.description: Settled stage: the cities and towns of a region, and how many of its persons live in them (society §5.2). The travel network of this stage has no parameters of its own: it connects the Prospects on show (§16).

CityShare.description: The share of the persons of a region that live in its cities, 0 to 1. A city stands on every Prospect on show for a city and on the capital of the region, and the cities share these persons by their rank. A region without a city keeps the share on the land, and every city holds at least one person where the region has one for it, so the share of a whole world lies near this number, not exactly on it. If the two shares sum to more than 1, both are scaled down (society §5.2).

TownShare.description: The share of the persons of a region that live in its towns, 0 to 1. A town stands on every other Prospect on show, and the towns share these persons by their rank. A region without a town keeps the share on the land, and every town holds at least one person where the region has one for it (society §5.2).

RankExponent.description: How unequal the cities and towns of a region are: the weight of a city or a town is its rank in the region raised to minus this. The capital has rank 1, then come the other cities, then the towns. With 1 the second city holds half the persons of the capital and the third a third; 0 gives all cities the same size and all towns the same size (society §5.2).

Housing.description: Housed stage: the households of the cities and towns of a region, those of the factions first (society §6).

FactionHouseholds.description: How many households a faction gets where the cities and towns of its region hold persons for them: at its seat first, then in the other cities and towns by rank. A faction has fewer where no fitting person is left (society §6).

FamilySizeWeights.description: The relative weight of each family size: the first number is for a family of 1 person, the second for 2 and so on. A family is never larger than the persons of its race that are left in its city or town (society §6).

TownWealth.description: The relative weight of each wealth level for a household of no faction in a town (society §6).

Destitute.description: Value for a Destitute household: it lives on alms or outside the law.

Poor.description: Value for a Poor household: unskilled labour.

Common.description: Value for a Common household: land or a simple trade.

Comfortable.description: Value for a Comfortable household: a skilled trade, a shop or a small office.

Rich.description: Value for a Rich household: capital, learning, high office or rule.

CityWealth.description: The relative weight of each wealth level for a household of no faction in a city (society §6).

Destitute.description: Value for a Destitute household: it lives on alms or outside the law.

Poor.description: Value for a Poor household: unskilled labour.

Common.description: Value for a Common household: land or a simple trade.

Comfortable.description: Value for a Comfortable household: a skilled trade, a shop or a small office.

Rich.description: Value for a Rich household: capital, learning, high office or rule.

FactionWealth.description: The relative weight of each wealth level for a household of a faction. The first household of the ruling faction is always Rich (society §6).

Destitute.description: Value for a Destitute household: it lives on alms or outside the law.

Poor.description: Value for a Poor household: unskilled labour.

Common.description: Value for a Common household: land or a simple trade.

Comfortable.description: Value for a Comfortable household: a skilled trade, a shop or a small office.

Rich.description: Value for a Rich household: capital, learning, high office or rule.

Servants.description: How many servants a household of each wealth level wants. It gets fewer where its city or town has too few persons left (society §6).

Destitute.description: Value for a Destitute household: it lives on alms or outside the law.

Poor.description: Value for a Poor household: unskilled labour.

Common.description: Value for a Common household: land or a simple trade.

Comfortable.description: Value for a Comfortable household: a skilled trade, a shop or a small office.

Rich.description: Value for a Rich household: capital, learning, high office or rule.

HeadAge.description: The age of the head of a household, in years: drawn evenly from this range (society §6).

MaleHeadChance.description: The chance that the head of a family of two or more persons is a man, 0 to 1. A person who is alone in its family is a man or a woman with even chance (society §6).

People.description: Peopled stage: the persons of every household, with their family relations and their vocations (society §7).

SpouseChance.description: The chance that the head of a family of two or more persons has a husband or a wife in the household, 0 to 1 (society §7).

WorkingAge.description: The age from which a person holds a vocation, in years. A younger person has none (society §7).

LandWorkFactor.description: The factor on the share of a vocation of the sector Land and water inside a city or a town: farmers, herders and fishers mostly live on the land. 1 gives them their full share, 0 keeps them out (society §7).

SameVocationChance.description: The chance that a person of the family other than the head holds the vocation of the head, 0 to 1. Otherwise the person gets a vocation of its own that fits the wealth of the household (society §7).

ServantVocation.description: The id of the vocation of a servant of a household. A servant has no vocation when the list of vocations has no such vocation or it is off (society §7).

Fields.description: The four Fields: noise maps that drive climate, biomes and resources. They have no stage (§9).

Precipitation.description: Precipitation in mm/yr, on a logarithmic scale. Its Distribution spreads the moisture classes of the biomes evenly: the points lie near the bounds between desert, steppe, sub-humid, humid and wet. Warped into belts. Feeds the biomes and thins the rivers of dry flat zones (§9, §13.2).

FeatureSizeKm.description: Size of the features of the noise in km: larger gives slower changes across the map.

Octaves.description: Number of noise octaves: a whole number, at least 1. More octaves add finer detail.

Lacunarity.description: Frequency multiplier from one octave to the next.

Gain.description: Amplitude multiplier from one octave to the next: lower makes the finer octaves weaker.

Min.description: The value at the strongest lows of the noise. At least 1 for the logarithmic Precipitation field.

Max.description: The value at the strongest highs of the noise. Only the strongest highs and lows reach Min and Max.

WarpKm.description: Strength of the warp in km: about the furthest the position the field is read at is moved. A warp of a few feature sizes draws the round features of the noise out into winding belts. 0 turns the warp off.

WarpFeatureSizeKm.description: Size of the features of the warp noise in km: larger gives longer, straighter belts. Only used when WarpKm is above 0.

Distribution.description: How the values are spread over the map: each point gives the share of the map that lies below a value. Min is the point at share 0 and Max the point at share 1, and a monotone spline runs through the points (through the logarithm of the values for Precipitation). The shares hold over a large area; a single view of the map can differ. Empty gives the bell shape of the noise: half the map lies in the middle quarter of the range between Min and Max (§9).

items.description: One point of the distribution of a field: the share of the map that lies below a value.

Share.description: Share of the map that lies below the value: above 0 and below 1. A point outside that is ignored.

Value.description: The value, in the unit of the field. Between Min and Max, and the values rise with the shares.

InitialTemperature.description: Initial Temperature in °C at sea level, on a linear scale, warped into belts. It is cooled by the height of the patch for the biomes. Its Distribution has one point at each bound between two thermal belts, so the shares are the shares of the belts at sea level (§9, §13.1, §13.2).

Gain.description: Amplitude multiplier from one octave to the next: lower makes the finer octaves weaker.

Max.description: The value at the strongest highs of the noise. Only the strongest highs and lows reach Min and Max.

Supernatural.description: Supernatural index, on a linear scale. Its Distribution keeps the supernatural rare: most of the map is low and 1 % lies above 80. It feeds the arcane materials of the resources, which lie only where it is above 60 (§14.1).

Bedrocks.description: The bedrock types and their relative weight under each elevation type. The bedrock of a zone is drawn by these weights (§14.1). The resource rules know the nine ids of the defaults; a bedrock with another id gives no bedrock-bound resources.

items.description: A bedrock type and its weight under each elevation type.

Id.description: The id the resource rules know the bedrock by: shield, foldBelt, granite, volcanic, basalt, ophiolite, carbonate, clastic or alluvium.

Name.description: The name shown for the bedrock.

Weights.description: Relative weight of the bedrock under each elevation type. Whole numbers; 0 means never under that type.

Description.description: What the bedrock is and what its land looks like: its rock, its landforms and what is dug from it (Appendix F). A picture of it is drawn from this text. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the bedrock: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Races.description: The races: the peoples that can live in the world. Add a race by adding an entry, and switch a race on or off with Enabled. The potential population of a region is shared between the races that are on, by their frequency in the biome of each patch and their height modifier at its height (society §2 and §3.2). A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A race: a people that can live in the world, and how frequent it is in each biome and at each height.

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the race by. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the race.

Enabled.description: Whether the race lives in the world. A race that is off gets no population, and the races that are on share the land without it.

BiomeFrequency.description: How frequent the race is in each biome, relative to the other races. The potential population of a patch is shared between the races that are on in proportion to these numbers, so only the proportions between the races within one biome matter. List only the biomes the race lives in: a biome that is left out has the frequency 0, and a frequency of 0 is not written to the file. A negative number counts as 0 (society §3.2).

TemperateMixedForest.description: Value for Temperate mixed forest patches.

TemperateBroadleafForest.description: Value for Temperate broadleaf forest patches.

TemperateRainForest.description: Value for Temperate rain forest patches.

TropicalDryForest.description: Value for Tropical dry forest patches.

TropicalRainForest.description: Value for Tropical rain forest patches.

Human.description: Whether the race is a human people. The name of a region is drawn from the word lists of the human races when the lead race of its ruling faction is human, and from the lists of the other races when it is not. Left out, the race is not human (society §2 and §4.10).

NameStyle.description: Which name model the names of the race are drawn from: Common (British given names and surnames), Exotic (elven) or Dark (dark elven). The surname of a house that rules a region comes from the model of its lead race, and the names of the persons of the race are meant to. Left out, the race uses Common (society §2, §4.10 and §7).

HeightModifier.description: How the height of the land changes the frequency of the race: control points from the mean height of a patch to a factor on its biome frequencies. The factor runs in a straight line between two points and is constant beyond the first and the last. Two points at the same height make a step: the first holds below that height, the second from that height and up. So [200 → 0, 200 → 1] is a race that only lives from 200 m and up, and [200 → 1, 200 → 0] one that only lives below 200 m. Left out, the height does not matter to the race (society §3.2).

items.description: One control point of the height modifier of a race: the factor at a height.

HeightM.description: Height in metres above sea level.

Factor.description: What the biome frequencies of the race are multiplied by at that height. 0 means the race does not live at that height; a negative number counts as 0.

FactionLeaning.description: How much the race leans to each type of faction, 0 to 3: 3 for the kind of group it forms first, 0 for a kind it never forms. It weighs the race in the draws for the type and the lead race of a faction. Left out, the race leans to every type alike (society §4.4).

Family.description: Value for the type Family: a house and its household.

Race.description: Value for the type Race: a people.

Vocation.description: Value for the type Vocation: a trade.

Belief.description: Value for the type Belief: a faith.

Magic.description: Value for the type Magic: the arcane.

Place.description: Value for the type Place: a town or a valley that rules itself.

AppreciatedRaces.description: The ids of the other races this race appreciates: peoples it trades with, lives well beside or looks up to. One-directional: the other race need not appreciate it back. Every id must be another race of the list, and no id may also stand in HatedRaces. Left out, the race appreciates no race in particular. No generation rule reads it yet; it is meant for the factions of a region (society §2).

HatedRaces.description: The ids of the other races this race hates: peoples it fears, fights or holds a grudge against. One-directional: the other race need not hate it back. Every id must be another race of the list, and no id may also stand in AppreciatedRaces. Left out, the race hates no race in particular. No generation rule reads it yet; it is meant for the factions of a region (society §2).

FavouriteColours.description: The ids of the favourite colours of the race, the dearest first: the colours of its dress, its banners and its goods. Every id must be a colour of the Colours list. The main and the secondary colour of a faction are drawn mostly from the favourite colours of its lead race, the first ones most often. Left out, the race has no favourite colour and its factions draw from every colour alike (society §2 and §4.9).

Description.description: What a person of the race looks like: build, skin, hair, eyes, dress and the marks that tell the race apart (society §2). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the race: where it comes from and what it tells about itself (society §2). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Vocations.description: The vocations: the work a person does, in nine sectors. Add a vocation by adding an entry, and switch one on or off with Enabled. The persons of the cities and towns get one (society §7); the vocations of the countryside are not drawn yet (society §8). A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A vocation: the work a person does. The persons of the cities and towns get one (society §7); the vocations of the countryside are not drawn yet (society §8).

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the vocation by. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the vocation.

Enabled.description: Whether the vocation exists in the world.

Sector.description: The sector of the vocation: one of nine (society §8).

LowestTier.description: The lowest tier of place in which the vocation is found: Countryside, Town, City or Capital (society §8).

SharePercent.description: The starting share of the labour force of a whole region that holds the vocation, in per cent. The shares of the defaults sum to 100. They are starting values, not tuned (society §8).

Standing.description: The social standing of the vocation, as a range on a scale of six: 1 outcast, 2 poor, 3 common, 4 middling, 5 wealthy, 6 ruling. The head of a household gets a vocation whose standing fits the wealth of the household: Destitute 1, Poor 2, Common 3, Comfortable 4, Rich 5 and 6 (society §7 and §8).

OnWater.description: Whether the vocation is only found in a place on water: the shipwright and the sailor (society §8).

Variants.description: The variants of the vocation: the smaller trades it covers, such as the shepherd of the herder and the armourer of the smith, each with a name, a description and a lore (society §8).

items.description: A variant of a vocation: a smaller trade it covers (society §8).

Name.description: The name of the variant, such as shepherd. Unique among the variants of its vocation.

Description.description: What the variant is: the work a person of it does, and what tells that person apart from the others of the vocation. A picture of it is drawn from this text. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the variant: its standing, its customs and its quarrels. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Description.description: What the vocation is: the work a person of it does (society §8). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the vocation: its standing, its customs and its quarrels (society §8). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Tools.description: The tools: the things the vocations work with. A tool lists the vocations that work with it by id, and its emblem weight says how well it serves as the emblem of a coat of arms. Tools are not drawn yet; the coats of arms of families, guilds and some cities are to take their charges from them (society §8.1). A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A tool: a thing a vocation works with, and the vocations that work with it. Tools are not drawn yet; they are meant for the coats of arms of families, guilds and some cities (society §8.1).

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the tool by, in camelCase like heavyPlough. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the tool.

Enabled.description: Whether the tool exists in the world. A tool that is off is no tool of any vocation.

Vocations.description: The ids of the vocations that work with the tool, the vocation it belongs to most first. Every id must be a vocation of the Vocations list, and a tool lists at least one (society §8.1).

EmblemWeight.description: How well the tool serves as the emblem of its vocations on a coat of arms, a banner or a sign: the weight it has when an emblem is drawn among the tools of a vocation. 0 means never: a tool that cannot be drawn as one plain figure, such as a kiln or a pit. The defaults run from 0 to 3, and 3 is the tool that is the sign of its trade, such as the anvil of the smith (society §8.1).

Description.description: What the tool is: its form, what it is made of and how it is used (society §8.1). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the tool: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it (society §8.1). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Colours.description: The colours: the named colours of cloth, paint and banners. A race lists its favourite colours by id, and a faction gets a main and a secondary colour from the list (society §4.9 and §9.1). Add a colour by adding an entry. A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A colour: a named colour of cloth, paint and banners. Races point at their favourite colours and factions at their main and secondary colour (society §9.1).

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the colour by, in camelCase like skyBlue. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the colour.

Hex.description: The colour as #RRGGBB: six hexadecimal digits after a #. It is what a picture shows, and its lightness decides which secondary colour stands out against a main colour (society §4.9).

Flora.description: The flora: the plants that can grow in the world. Every patch gets a few of the kinds that fit its biome (§13.4). A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A kind of flora: a plant that can grow in the world, and the biomes it grows in.

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the kind by. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the kind.

Type.description: The type of the kind: Tree, Shrub, Flower, Herb, Fruit, Grass, Vine, Fungus, Moss, Aquatic or Arcane.

Enabled.description: Whether the kind grows in the world. A kind that is off is never drawn for a patch.

Biomes.description: The biomes the kind grows in. A land patch can only get a kind that lists its biome (§13.4).

Sea.description: Whether the kind grows in the sea: an ocean patch can only get a kind that is of the sea (§13.4).

Frequency.description: How frequent the kind is, relative to the other kinds that fit a patch. A kind with twice the frequency is drawn about twice as often. 0 or below means never (§13.4).

MinSupernatural.description: The Supernatural (0 to 100) a patch needs for the kind to grow there. 0 means anywhere. The arcane plants of the defaults need 60, 75 or 90 (§13.4).

StandsInFor.description: The type of flora the kind stands in for. A patch that gets the kind gets no kind of that type: the giant mushrooms of the defaults stand in for the trees. Left out means the kind stands in for nothing (§13.4).

Description.description: What the kind is: its form, its size, where it grows and what it is used for (§13.4). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the kind: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it (§13.4). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Fauna.description: The fauna: the creatures that can live in the world. Every patch gets a few of the kinds that fit its biome (§13.4). A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A kind of fauna: a creature that can live in the world, and the biomes it lives in.

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the kind by. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the kind.

Type.description: The type of the kind: Critter (small), Animal (ordinary wildlife and livestock), Beast (large or dangerous) or Monster (supernatural or legendary).

Enabled.description: Whether the kind lives in the world. A kind that is off is never drawn for a patch.

Biomes.description: The biomes the kind lives in. A land patch can only get a kind that lists its biome (§13.4).

Sea.description: Whether the kind lives in the sea: an ocean patch can only get a kind that is of the sea (§13.4).

Frequency.description: How frequent the kind is, relative to the other kinds that fit a patch. A kind with twice the frequency is drawn about twice as often. 0 or below means never (§13.4).

MinSupernatural.description: The Supernatural (0 to 100) a patch needs for the kind to live there. 0 means anywhere. The monsters of the defaults need 60, 75 or 90 (§13.4).

Description.description: What the kind is: its form, its size, where it lives and how it behaves (§13.4). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the kind: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it (§13.4). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Resources.description: The resources: the name, the description and the lore of each of the 27 generated resources and of their variants (§14 and Appendix G.3). The list only holds texts: which resource and which variant a patch gets is decided by the resource rules, and a resource or a variant that is left out has no texts. A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: The texts of one generated resource and of its variants (§14 and Appendix G.3).

Resource.description: The resource the texts belong to: one of the 27 generated resources.

Name.description: The name shown for the resource.

Description.description: What the resource is: what it looks like as a good, raw and as it is traded (§14). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the resource: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it (§14). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Variants.description: The variants of the resource, by the name the resource rules give them, such as rye for grain and star metal for the arcane materials (Appendices B and D).

items.description: The texts of one variant of a resource.

Name.description: The name of the variant, exactly as the resource rules give it: the texts are found by it.

Description.description: What the variant is: what it looks like, raw and as it is traded (§14). A picture of it is drawn from this text, so an invented one needs it to look the same every time. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the variant: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it (§14). No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

items.description: The texts of one biome (§13).

Biome.description: The biome the texts belong to.

Name.description: The name shown for the biome.

Description.description: What the land of the biome looks like: its ground, its plant cover and its light. A picture of it is drawn from this text. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.

Lore.description: The lore of the biome: what the peoples of the world make of it and tell about it. No generation rule reads it. The text "**missing description**" marks one that is not written yet.
